objectives: I can identify the passive voice in spoken and written sentences.
I can form passive sentences using is/are + past participle.
I can describe what is made or done in a school or media context using the passive voice.

stages.name: Opening — Retrieval and Bridge
stages.purpose: Activate prior knowledge of past tense verb forms and subject-verb agreement — the building blocks pupils need to form the passive.

procedure.text: Quick-fire oral recall (whole class). Ask in sequence: 'Past tense of make?' (made) / 'Past tense of film?' (filmed) / 'True or false: They shows the documentary.' (False — shows must be show).
Think-write: 'Write the past tense of these four verbs — produce, edit, broadcast, perform.' Then: 'Turn this into a question: They film documentaries here.'
Partner swap and check. Answers: produced / edited / broadcast / performed. Question: Do they film documentaries here?

Bridge (2 min): 'You just said what people do. But sometimes we do not know — or do not care — who does the action. In German you say Der Film wird gedreht. English works the same way: The film is filmed. The thing that receives the action comes first. That is what we learn today.' Write on board: I can describe what is made or done using the passive voice (e.g. The film is made in a studio).

stages.name: Grammar Input — Passive Voice
stages.purpose: Introduce the passive voice rule (be + past participle) with before-and-after examples in a media and school context.

procedure.text: Display the grammar card. Read the rule aloud. Point to the form: thing + is/are + past participle. Highlight the German contrast: is/are, NOT becomes.
Work through the four before/after examples on the grammar card together. For each: read the active sentence, then the passive. Ask: 'What moved to the front?'
Choral drill: pupils repeat each passive sentence after you.

Mini check: say two active sentences aloud, pupils call out the passive. 'They create the show in Berlin.' → The show is created in Berlin. / 'They release the film on Friday.' → The film is released on Friday.

stages.name: Guided Practice — Gap-fill
stages.purpose: Consolidate passive form through supported written practice using media vocabulary.

procedure.text: Hand out or display the gap-fill exercise. Explain: each blank needs the passive form of the verb shown in brackets. Remind: is for one thing, are for more than one.
Go through answers together. Write correct forms on the board. Pause on any sentence where more than two pupils had errors and repeat the rule.

stages.name: Production — School sentences
stages.purpose: Move from controlled practice to free production in a familiar context, using passive voice to describe real school routines.

procedure.text: Write sentence frame on board: In our school, ___ is/are ___ (past participle) every day/week/year. Example: The classroom is cleaned every day. / Homework is given every week.
Pupils write 4 passive sentences about their own school. They may use any topic: lessons, rooms, equipment, events.
Partner check: partner reads each sentence and checks — is/are correct? Past participle correct? Mark any errors.
2 or 3 pupils share one sentence with the class. Correct together if needed.

stages.name: Wrap-up — Exit ticket
stages.purpose: Collect quick written evidence of each pupil's passive voice production to inform the next lesson.

procedure.text: Exit ticket: pupils write 2 passive sentences on a slip of paper — topic is free (school, home, TV, sport). Collect before they leave.
Preview: 'Next lesson we practice passive with more vocabulary and look at how to add by to say who does the action.'

differentiationNotes: Weaker pupils: word bank remains visible during gap-fill (produced, are printed, is filmed, is written, is published, are performed, is translated, are edited); sentence frame stays on board throughout Stage 4. Stronger pupils: Stage 4 extension task — write 2 extra sentences using by (e.g. The news is broadcast by the BBC.) and share with a different partner.
exercisePlan: gap_fill — 8 passive voice sentences using m1 media vocabulary (broadcast, print, film, write, publish, perform, translate, edit) — saved
